# Ticket paraphrases generated by Codex (declared deviation)

**What:** the 15 paraphrase slots `scenario/tasks/<ticket>.p1.md … p5.md` for `X-rename`, `X-remove` and `X-api`. In every cell of these tickets with N = 10 at wording W1 (P1, P2, P5, and P6 if it is generated) the manifest gives round r the slot p((r − 1) mod 5 + 1), so each cell runs each paraphrase twice instead of the base text ten times ("fallacy of the single text"). P0, Pilot X1 and W2 always use the base text.

**Deviation from spec §6.1.** The spec asked for paraphrases written by a person (Alfredo or a colleague), so that they would not come from the same model that is measured. They were generated by a model instead:

- **Origin:** Codex (`gpt-5.6-terra`, reasoning effort medium), 2026-10-11. It was given only the three base ticket texts (below), in an empty folder without access to this repository, the scenario, the context files or the consumers, and asked for 8 candidate paraphrases per ticket that keep the instruction and the field names.
- **Selection:** 8 candidates per ticket (24). In the design session the 9 listed below were discarded by hand (near-identical to the base text, redundant with another kept one, awkward, or drifting towards the outcome-based wording W2 of RQ5). Alfredo approved the remaining 5 per ticket; their slot order is the order below.
- **Conflict of interest:** Codex is itself a measured unit (Pilot X1 `x1c-*`, and P6 if it runs). For the confirmatory runs (`cc-sonnet`, Claude Code + Sonnet) there is no conflict: the paraphrases do not come from the measured model. For Codex runs it is a declared threat: in P6 the Codex unit receives, in its N = 10 cells (the core P1 and P2 cells), ticket texts written by its own model family; its N = 5 cells and Pilot X1 (`x1c-*`) use the base text.

Base texts (W1, unchanged):

- `X-rename`: Clean up the OrderPlaced event: rename totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt, so the event matches the naming used by the Payments and Customer APIs.
- `X-remove`: Remove the unused field channel from the OrderPlaced event and from the order model. Nothing reads it anymore.
- `X-api`: Simplify the response of GET /orders/{id}: return the order lines as items instead of lines, to match the naming used in the rest of our APIs.

## Kept (15)

### X-rename
| Slot | Text |
|---|---|
| p1 | The OrderPlaced event uses different names from the Payments and Customer APIs. Rename totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt. |
| p2 | To match the naming used by the Payments and Customer APIs, update the OrderPlaced event fields totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt. |
| p3 | Update the OrderPlaced event by changing totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt; this brings its naming in line with the Payments and Customer APIs. |
| p4 | The OrderPlaced event should use the same naming as the Payments and Customer APIs. Rename totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt. |
| p5 | Change the OrderPlaced event names totalCents and placedAt to amountCents and createdAt, respectively, so they match the Payments and Customer APIs. |

### X-remove
| Slot | Text |
|---|---|
| p1 | The channel field is unused, as nothing reads it anymore. Remove it from the OrderPlaced event and the order model. |
| p2 | Nothing reads channel anymore, so remove it from both the OrderPlaced event and the order model. |
| p3 | Since channel is no longer read, remove that field from the OrderPlaced event and from the order model. |
| p4 | The OrderPlaced event and order model still have a channel field that nothing reads anymore; remove it from both. |
| p5 | Drop channel from the OrderPlaced event and order model, since nothing reads the field anymore. |

### X-api
| Slot | Text |
|---|---|
| p1 | GET /orders/{id} returns lines under that name, unlike the rest of our APIs. Return them as items instead. |
| p2 | To match naming in the rest of our APIs, have GET /orders/{id} return the order lines as items rather than lines. |
| p3 | Change the GET /orders/{id} response to call the order lines items, matching the naming used in the rest of our APIs. |
| p4 | Use items instead of lines for the order lines in GET /orders/{id}, matching the naming used across the rest of our APIs. |
| p5 | In GET /orders/{id}, name the returned order lines items rather than lines so the response matches the naming in the rest of our APIs. |

## Discarded (9)

| Ticket | Candidate | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| X-rename | Rename totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt in the OrderPlaced event so its naming matches the Payments and Customer APIs. | near-identical to the base text |
| X-rename | Make the OrderPlaced event consistent with the Payments and Customer APIs: call totalCents amountCents and placedAt createdAt. | ambiguous; close to W2 |
| X-rename | Align the OrderPlaced event's field names with the Payments and Customer APIs by renaming totalCents to amountCents and placedAt to createdAt. | close to W2 |
| X-remove | Remove channel from the OrderPlaced event and the order model; nothing reads this field anymore. | near-identical to the base text |
| X-remove | Remove the unused channel field in the OrderPlaced event and the order model. Nothing reads it anymore. | near-identical to the base text |
| X-remove | Nothing reads the channel field anymore. Delete it from the OrderPlaced event and the order model. | redundant with p2 |
| X-api | Return the order lines as items in GET /orders/{id} to match the naming used in the rest of our APIs. | near-identical to the base text |
| X-api | The rest of our APIs use items for this naming. In GET /orders/{id}, return the order lines as items instead of lines. | awkward |
| X-api | Simplify GET /orders/{id} by returning the order lines as items instead of lines, as in the rest of our APIs. | near-identical to the base text |

The files contain exactly the kept text, one line, no marker; `harness.scenario_io.paraphrases_ready` is true for the three tickets and `results/real/manifest.json` records `"p1..p5 x2"` for each. Declared in `PREREGISTRATION.md` §3, `scenario/README.md` and `docs/DECISIONS.md`.
